title: Chicken Burrito with Beans, Rice and Cheese

content.title: About
content.content: A chicken burrito with beans, rice and cheese is a classic Mexican dish consisting of a large flour tortilla wrapped around a filling of seasoned grilled chicken, cooked rice, black beans, melted cheese and often topped with salsa, sour cream or guacamole.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Burritos originated in northern Mexico where wheat flour was more available than corn.
Chicken is usually marinated in chili, cumin and lime for a distinctive flavor.
Black beans used in the filling are high in protein and fiber, making the burrito more nutritious.
Cheese in traditional burritos is often shredded cheddar or Mexican queso fresco, which melts easily.
Burritos are commonly served with fresh salsa, guacamole or sour cream for added freshness and creaminess.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Chicken provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Rice and beans supply slowly digestible carbohydrates for sustained energy.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Black beans are a good source of fiber, supporting digestive health.

items.title: Calcium and phosphorus
items.content: Cheese adds calcium and phosphorus, important for bone and teeth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken and beans provide B6 and folate, which aid metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The combination of cheese, sour cream and flour tortilla can make the burrito calorie‑dense, so portion control is advised.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Salt in sauces and cheese can increase sodium intake, which may be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger allergic reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or dairy protein allergy.

items.title: Gluten in the tortilla
items.content: Traditional flour tortillas contain gluten, making the dish unsuitable for people with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Burritos are typically eaten by hand, often cut in half for easier handling. Warm it in a microwave or skillet until the cheese melts. Add fresh salsa, guacamole or sour cream to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store a prepared burrito in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For freezing, wrap tightly in plastic film and keep in the freezer for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before eating.
